---
title: 'Mobile design language'
description: 'How redesigned mobile mini apps look and behave: type, surfaces, colour roles, motion, page anatomy, patterns, responsive rules and per-app identity, built on the shared composition kit.'
---

This page is the visual and interaction contract for the mobile app redesign.
The [design system](/build/development-tools/mobile-design-system) owns the
layout primitives, tokens, components and overlays; this page says how to
compose them so every mini app feels like one product without looking like a
copy of the next one.

The language grew out of the Settings redesign: translucent grouped cards
over the appearance theme, soft tinted icon tiles, generous rounding and
muted captions. Home and Notifications extended it with tones, icon tiles,
grouped rows and shared states. Mini apps now adopt the same vocabulary
through the composition kit in `package:mobile/core/ui/kit/kit.dart`.

## Principles

1. **Lead with the answer.** A root page opens with what matters now (a
   balance, the next meeting, today's tasks), not with a toolbar or a list
   header.
2. **One surface family.** Content sits on grouped cards, panels and stat
   tiles that share radii, borders and translucency, so appearance themes
   (solid, gradient, blobs) show through consistently.
3. **Theme roles only.** Every colour comes from `AppColorTokens` through an
   `AppTone`. No hex values, `Colors.*` hues or per-feature palettes.
4. **Cheap by default.** Static fills and borders, no blur behind scrolling
   content, no shadows on list items, no layers for opacity.
5. **Adaptive, not stretched.** Wider bodies get more columns, side panels and
   two panes, never a phone layout scaled up.
6. **Accessible without exceptions.** 48dp targets, readable contrast in every
   theme, unclamped text scaling and complete semantics.

## Typography

Use `AppTokens.of(context).typography` (`context.tokens.typography`). Styles
carry no colour; apply a role from the colour tokens.

| Role | Style | Use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Hero figure | `x3Large` w700, tabular figures, -0.4 tracking | `AppSummaryHero` headline |
| Stat value | `x2Large` w700, tabular figures | `AppStatTile` value |
| Section title | `large` w600 | `AppSectionHeader` |
| Panel and row title | `base` w600 | `AppPanel`, `AppRichRow` |
| Grouped row title | `base` w500 | `AppGroupedRow` |
| Body and supporting | `small`, `mutedForeground`, 1.35–1.4 height | subtitles, messages |
| Meta and captions | `xSmall` w500, `mutedForeground` | `AppMetaItem`, trends |
| Grouped caption | `labelLarge` w600 | `AppSectionCaption` |

- Numbers that update or line up (amounts, counts, times) use
  `FontFeature.tabularFigures()`.
- Titles wrap to two lines before truncating. Never clamp
  `MediaQuery.textScaler`; components grow vertically instead.
- The shell's top navbar owns the page title. Do not repeat it as a heading
  in the body; the hero or the first section header introduces the content.

## Spacing, radius and elevation

Spacing uses the 4pt `AppSpacing` scale and the page tokens in
`AppLayout`. Composition rules on top of those tokens:

| Between | Gap |
| --- | --- |
| Hero and first section | `AppLayout.sectionGap` (24) |
| Sections | `AppLayout.sectionGap` (24) |
| Section header and its content | 12 (built into `AppSectionHeader`) |
| Tiles in a grid, stacked cards | `AppLayout.itemGap` (12) |
| Rows inside a card | hairline divider, no gap |

| Surface | Radius | Elevation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Grouped card, panel, hero | `AppRadius.card` (22) | none |
| Stat tile, grid tile | 20 | none |
| Filter pill, badge | pill | none |
| Sheet | `AppRadius.sheet` (24) | overlay shadow from the host |
| Dock | `AppRadius.dock` (26) | owned by the shell |

Elevation is reserved for floating layers (dock, sheets, dialogs, toasts).
Cards in lists separate with a border and the surface tint, never with a
shadow. Legacy `FinancePanel` adds a 28px blurred shadow to every card; new
code uses `AppPanel` instead.

## Surfaces

| Surface | Fill | Border | When |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Page | appearance background (solid, gradient or blobs) | none | owned by the shell |
| Grouped card (`AppGroupedCard`) | `surface` at 72% | `outlineVariant` 40% | lists of rows |
| Panel (`AppPanel`) | `card` at 86% | `border` 70% | charts, breakdowns, short lists, inline forms |
| Stat tile (`AppStatTile`) | `card` at 86% | `border` 70% | key figures |
| Hero (`AppSummaryHero`) | tone fill blended into `card`, linear gradient | tone at 18% | the opening summary |

All of them become solid when the platform requests high contrast
(`MediaQuery.highContrastOf`).

## Colour roles

Colours come from `AppColorTokens`, which the appearance theme resolves for
every theme, accent and brightness. Components choose an `AppTone`, and the
tone resolves a foreground and a quiet fill:

| Tone | Foreground role | Fill | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `neutral` | `mutedForeground` | `muted` | default, inactive |
| `primary` | `primary` (follows the accent) | primary at 12% (20% dark) | the app's main object |
| `info` | `info` | info tint | time, schedule, links |
| `success` | `success` | success tint | money in, done, healthy |
| `warning` | `warning` | warning tint | due soon, attention |
| `destructive` | `destructive` | destructive tint | overdue, failed, money out over budget |

- Text that carries meaning (values, titles) stays in `foreground`. Tones
  colour icons, meters, trend labels and small accents, which keeps every
  theme above WCAG AA for text.
- Tone tints are fills behind icons, not backgrounds behind body text.
- `primary` follows the user's accent. Do not assume it is blue; in Classic
  it is near-black in light mode and near-white in dark mode.
- Per-module hex palettes (the Apps hub cards, Drive's green, finance
  positive/negative literals) are migration debt; map them to tones.

## Iconography

- Use the generated Lucide icons (`LucideIcons`, `LucideLabIcons`, `AppIcons`)
  so mobile matches the web glyph for glyph. Material `Icons.*` are legacy.
- Icons sit in an `AppIconTile` when they identify an object (a row, a stat,
  an eyebrow) and stand alone when they decorate metadata (`AppMetaItem`,
  14dp) or controls (16–20dp).
- Row tiles are 32dp in grouped rows and 40dp in rich rows. Stat and hero
  eyebrow tiles are 28dp.
- Icons never carry meaning alone. Pair them with a label or a semantics
  label, and give icon buttons a tooltip.

## Motion

Motion explains a change; it never decorates a resting screen.

| Use | Duration | Curve |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Press, toggle, selection | `AppMotion.fast` (120ms) | `standard` |
| Expand, swap content, sheet content | `AppMotion.normal` (220ms) | `standard` |
| Page-level or large layout change | `AppMotion.slow` (320ms) | `standard` |

**Cheap-animation policy.** These rules keep the kit fast on mid-range
Android devices; the Android jank lane may add a user-facing "reduce effects"
switch on top of them.

- Animate transforms and colours of small subtrees. Do not animate
  `Opacity` over large subtrees; use `FadeTransition` or an animated colour.
- No live `BackdropFilter` behind scrolling content. Frosted chrome goes
  through the shell's glass policy, which draws near-opaque fills on Android.
- No `ShaderMask`, `ColorFiltered` or `Opacity` wrappers that force a
  `saveLayer` in lists. Fade edges with a painted gradient or not at all.
- No shadows on list items or tiles. `AppElevation.raised` is for single
  floating cards only.
- Wrap independently repainting regions (a ticking timer, a live meter, a
  chart) in a `RepaintBoundary`. `SliverAppAdaptiveGrid` adds one per tile.
- Skeletons are static shapes. Do not add shimmer.
- Respect `MediaQuery.disableAnimationsOf`: skip to the end state.

## Page anatomy

A redesigned mini-app root page reads top to bottom:

1. **Shell header.** Title and actions from the shell. No body AppBar.
2. **Summary hero** (`AppSummaryHero`) or a **stat row**
   (`AppAdaptiveGrid` of `AppStatTile`, `equalHeight: true`). Pick one per
   page, not both stacked at the same weight.
3. **Filter bar** (`AppFilterBar`) when the list has 2–6 views. Search is the
   shell search action. More than six filters belong in a sheet.
4. **Sections.** `AppSectionHeader` plus content: grouped rows, rich rows,
   panels or a grid.
5. **End clearance.** Handled by the page primitives.

Detail pages drop the hero, open with the object's title block and use
`AppPanel` with `AppKeyValueRow`s for properties. Forms use
`AppGroupedSection`s and open with `showAppSheet` or as a full-screen route
above the shell.

## Patterns

### Section headers

`AppSectionHeader(title:, count:, subtitle:, actionLabel:, onAction:)` heads
content sections (lists, grids, panels). The quieter `AppSectionCaption` (via
`AppGroupedSection.caption`) heads settings-style groups. Use one style per
page level; never stack a caption under a section header.

### Lists and rows

| Need | Component |
| --- | --- |
| Settings, navigation, simple items | `AppGroupedRow` in an `AppGroupedCard` |
| Entities with metadata (transactions, files, customers, products, courses) | `AppRichRow` with `AppMetaItem`s |
| Long homogeneous collections | `AppPageListView.builder` of rich rows wrapped in `AppGroupedSlice`s; group by date or status with section headers |

- Rich rows put a value or a status `AppBadge` on the trailing edge and a
  unit or time in `trailingCaption`.
- `selected: true` marks the open item when a list drives a detail pane.
- Show at most three `AppMetaItem`s. Overdue or failing facts take the
  `destructive` role colour, everything else stays muted.
- Group long lists by meaning (Today / Yesterday / Earlier, Overdue / Next /
  Later) instead of one undifferentiated column.

### Cards and grids

- `AppAdaptiveGrid(minTileWidth:, maxColumns:)` lays out summaries and small
  collections; `SliverAppAdaptiveGrid` lays out long collections lazily with a
  fixed tile height scaled by text size.
- Default stat tiles use `minTileWidth: 160` (two per phone, four on a
  tablet). Catalogues and drives use 120–180 depending on thumbnail size.
- `AppPanel(title:, subtitle:, actionLabel:)` frames a chart, breakdown or
  short list. Set `padded: false` when the child brings row insets.

### Stat tiles and charts

- A stat tile shows one label, one value and at most one context line
  (`trend` or `caption`) plus an optional `progress` meter.
- `AppStatTrend(positive:)` decides the colour, not the direction: a falling
  expense is good news.
- `AppMeter` is the static progress bar for budgets, goals, quotas and
  streaks.
- Charts live in an `AppPanel`, use tone foregrounds for series (at most four
  series per chart), label axes in `xSmall` muted text and keep values in
  tabular figures. Paint charts with `CustomPainter` inside a
  `RepaintBoundary`; do not animate them on scroll.

### Filters, search and sort

- `AppFilterBar<T>` is a single-select pill row for views of the same list
  (All / Open / Done). Counts sit inside the pill.
- `AppSegmentedControl<T>` switches between two to four modes of the same
  content (Day / Week / Month, Self / Team). It is not a filter: use it for
  view modes and scopes, never for more than four choices.
- Sorting and scopes (a collection, a wallet) use an `AppFilterButton` that
  names the current choice, opens an `AppOptionTile` sheet and shows `active`
  while it narrows the list.
- Search uses the shell search action (`AppSheetSearch` in sheets). Do not put
  an inline search field above a list inside the shell.
- Multi-select filters (labels, people, ranges) open a sheet and show their
  active state as a count on a filter button.

### Empty, loading and error states

- First load: `AppSkeletonRows` inside the same card the rows will occupy, or
  static tile shapes for grids. No spinners in the middle of a page.
- Empty: `AppStateMessage` with an icon, a title that says what is missing, a
  message that says what will appear here and one action that fixes it.
- Error with no data: `AppStateMessage(tone: AppTone.destructive)` with a
  retry action.
- Error with cached data: keep the data and show `AppStateMessage.inline`
  above it ("Could not refresh, showing data from 10:24").
- Load more: load automatically at the end of the list. Show a skeleton row,
  not a "Load more" button.

### Forms and sheets

- Open forms with `showAppSheet` and lay them out with `AppSheetScaffold` and
  `AppGroupedSection`s of `AppTextField`, `AppSelect`, `AppSwitch`,
  `AppDatePicker` and `AppTimePicker`. Do not use `AlertDialog`,
  `SwitchListTile`, `showDatePicker` or raw `showModalBottomSheet`.
- Confirmations use `showAppDialog` with a destructive `AppButton` for
  destructive actions.
- One primary action per sheet, in the sheet's action area.

## Responsive rules

Decisions use the width the page body receives (after the shell rail), via
`DeviceClass` and the page primitives.

| Body width | Navigation | Layout |
| --- | --- | --- |
| compact (< 600) | dock | one column; hero full width; stat grid 2 columns; lists full width |
| medium (600–839) | dock | hero facts beside the headline; stat grid 3–4 columns; grids 3–4 columns; list/detail stays push-based unless the app needs a split |
| expanded (≥ 840) | rail | `AppPageKind.root` pages use 2-column section layouts (list plus side panel); entity lists split into list/detail with `AppMasterDetail`; grids 4–6 columns |

- Use the shared list/detail primitive, `AppMasterDetail`
  (`core/layout/master_detail.dart`), for two-pane screens. Do not build a
  per-feature split.
- Side panels (filters, an inspector, a summary) sit on the trailing side at
  320–360dp and scroll independently.
- Pointer devices get hover states from `InkWell` and tooltips on icon
  buttons; keyboard users get focus rings from the core controls.

## Visual identity per app

"Not repetitive" means each app has a recognisable opening and rhythm while
sharing the same parts. Identity comes from four levers, in this order:

1. **The hero question.** Each root answers its own question in the hero:
   Finance "How much do I have?", Calendar "What is next?", Habits "Am I on
   streak?". Never reuse the same eyebrow and layout across apps.
2. **The app tone.** One `AppTone` per app for the hero, its icon tiles and
   meters. Other tones only appear for status.
3. **The dominant pattern.** Pick the layout that fits the data: a timeline
   for Calendar, a board for Tasks, a ledger of rich rows for Finance, a
   catalogue grid for Inventory, a gallery for Drive.
4. **Signature detail.** One small, cheap flourish per app, such as a streak
   meter in Habits, a live dot on the next meeting in Meet or a storage meter
   in Drive.

| App | Tone | Hero question | Dominant pattern | Signature detail |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Tasks | `primary` | What should I do today? | grouped rich rows, board on wide | due-state meta in role colours |
| Calendar | `info` | What is next? | agenda timeline | now-line and next-event card |
| Time tracker | `info` | What am I working on? | running timer hero, session list | single repainting ticker |
| Habits | `success` | Am I on streak? | tracker cards with meters | streak meter |
| Notes | `warning` | What was I thinking? | masonry cards | pinned strip |
| Finance | `success` | How much do I have? | ledger of rich rows | budget meters |
| Inventory | `primary` | What needs restocking? | catalogue grid | low-stock badges |
| CRM | `info` | Who needs attention? | people rich rows | relationship meta |
| Education | `primary` | What do I teach next? | course cards grid | progress meters |
| Drive | `info` | Where is my file? | file gallery and list | storage meter |
| Documents | `neutral` | What was I writing? | recent strip and list | reading-width editor |
| CMS | `info` | What is ready to publish? | pipeline queues and a status-toned library | per-collection publish meters |
| Chat | `primary` | Who is waiting for me? | conversations list, two-pane | unread emphasis |
| Meet | `success` | When is my next call? | up-next hero and grid | live dot and Join |
| Apps hub | per app tone | Where do I go? | launcher grid by category | live badges |

The hub's tiles take each app's tone, so the launcher previews the identity
users meet inside the app.

## Composition kit

`package:mobile/core/ui/kit/kit.dart` exports:

| Widget | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `AppSummaryHero`, `AppHeroFact` | opening summary with tone, headline, facts and actions |
| `AppSectionHeader` | content section title with count, subtitle and action |
| `AppStatTile`, `AppStatTrend` | key figure with icon, trend, caption and meter |
| `AppMeter` | static progress bar |
| `AppPanel` | titled content surface |
| `AppKeyValueRow` | label and value on detail screens |
| `AppFilterBar`, `AppFilterOption`, `AppFilterButton` | single-select views, and the trailing sort or scope control |
| `AppSegmentedControl`, `AppSegment` | two to four equal-width modes of the same content |
| `AppGroupedSlice`, `AppSlicePosition` | one row's share of a grouped card in a lazy builder list |
| `AppRichRow`, `AppMetaItem` | entity row with metadata, trailing value and selection |
| `AppAdaptiveGrid`, `SliverAppAdaptiveGrid` | width-driven columns for summaries and collections |

Rows, tones, icon tiles and states (`AppGroupedRow`, `AppTone`,
`AppIconTile`, `AppSkeletonRows`, `AppStateMessage`) live in
`package:mobile/core/layout/layout.dart`.

### Migrating from `finance_ui.dart`

`features/finance/widgets/finance_ui.dart` grew into an informal shared kit
used by about 30 files outside Finance. Replace it as each app is redesigned:

| Legacy | Kit |
| --- | --- |
| `FinancePanel` | `AppPanel` (no shadow) or `AppGroupedCard` |
| `FinanceSectionHeader` | `AppSectionHeader` |
| `FinanceStatChip` | `AppStatTile` or `AppHeroFact` |
| `FinanceEmptyState` | `AppStateMessage` |
| `FinanceSkeletonBlock` | `AppSkeletonRows` |
| `FinanceKeyValueRow` | `AppKeyValueRow` |
| `FinancePalette` colours | `AppTone` roles |

## Pilot: CMS

The CMS mini app is the first app rebuilt entirely on the kit
(`features/cms`). Use it as the reference when redesigning another app.

- **Overview.** `AppSummaryHero` answers "what is ready to publish?" with
  the published share, drafts and scheduled counts, three facts and the two
  create actions. The three queues (needs attention, scheduled soon, archived
  backlog) are section headers over grouped cards of `AppRichRow`s and sit
  side by side on wide bodies through `AppAdaptiveGrid`. An `AppPanel`
  shows publish meters per collection. Tapping a queued item opens its entry.
- **Library.** A lazy list of `AppGroupedSlice`s: collections first, then
  entries with an `AppFilterBar` of statuses (with counts) and an
  `AppFilterButton` that picks the collection. Rows open their editor;
  delete moved from inline icon buttons into the editor.
- **States.** First load shows a static skeleton shaped like the overview.
  A denied workspace shows an `AppStateMessage`; a failed first load shows
  a destructive message with Retry; a failed refresh keeps the content under
  an inline notice. Empty queues and empty filters use inline messages.
- **Editors.** `AppSheetScaffold` forms with captioned sections,
  `AppTextField`, `AppSelect` and `AppToggleRow`. Save is the primary action
  and shows progress; Delete appears for existing items and asks for
  confirmation in an `AppDialog`. The collection Enabled switch appears only
  when editing, because creation always enables a collection. An entry keeps
  its collection after creation. Drafts and inline errors survive a failed
  save, as before.
- **Status language.** Every entry status has one tone and icon: draft
  `warning`, scheduled `info`, published `success`, archived `neutral`.

`test/features/cms/view/cms_render_test.dart` renders the overview and the
library at every review size and theme with the same guidelines as the kit
gallery. Feature render tests should use the shared harness in
`test/helpers/design_render_harness.dart` (`DesignRender`,
`DesignRenderApp`).

## Regression coverage

- `test/core/ui/kit/kit_components_test.dart` covers grid columns, filter
  and segment selection semantics, section header actions, trend colours,
  selected rows, slice positions, meter clamping, the hero's wide layout and
  high-contrast surfaces.
- `test/core/ui/kit/kit_gallery_test.dart` renders every component on three
  boards at 390x844, 820x1180 and 1440x900 in light, dark and Aurora blobs.
  Each render must lay out without exceptions and pass the tap-target,
  labelled-target and text-contrast guidelines. Set `DESIGN_RENDER_DIR` (and
  optionally `DESIGN_RENDER_PIXEL_RATIO`) to write the PNGs for review.
